accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE National Curriculum (2013) Year 1 mathematics, Measurement statutory requirement: 'sequence events in chronological order using language [for example, before and after, next, first, today, yesterday, tomorrow, morning, afternoon and evening]'; every one of those ten words is taught in the kid text or the lab. Day order morning, afternoon, evening and 'yesterday = the day before today, tomorrow = the day after' are stated exactly. p2 (n-k, 6-1=5 down to 4-3=1), p3 (d+1), m5 (d+w) and m7 (d-1 with d from 2) are whole and positive at every range corner.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the order-of-mention error (Clark 1971: young children act out 'before/after' sentences in the order the clauses are spoken), in step 2 with 'Before you put on your shoes, put on your socks' and 'Eat your lunch after you wash your hands', p4, m4 and challenge 'heard'; the skipped afternoon (step 3 prediction 'Evening', challenge 'skip' and 'night'); yesterday/tomorrow swaps (step 4 prediction 'Yesterday', m1, challenge 'tomorrow' and 'today'); and irreversible story order (snowman melts last, challenge 'any').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagorder is the only lab where the child drags drawn picture cards into time slots whose labels are the time words themselves (First/Next/Last, First/Then, Morning/Afternoon/Evening with a moving sun, Yesterday/Today/Tomorrow). flagclock reads clock hands and flagtally builds charts; no other lab sequences events. The 30% shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each scene only completes when every card is in the right slot; a wrong full row bounces the misplaced cards back with that card's own reason (for example 'You hear eat first, but you do it second'), so the child discovers the order by trying. The before/after scene reads the sentence on the canvas with the misleading word order kept, and the snowman story adds a fourth slot so first/next/then/last is used in full.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with the tempting wrong answer young children give: 'Before you put on your shoes, put on your socks. What do you do first?' (Shoes, the word heard first), 'What comes straight after morning?' (Evening) and 'Your party is the day after today. When is it?' (Yesterday). Each is tested straight away when the cards are placed.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with rotated answer order and 12 m= messages, one per wrong pick (skip, night, heard, off, tomorrow, today, any, night2, eve, lunch, flower, same), each naming the slip, e.g. 'Tuesday is tomorrow, the day after today. Yesterday was the day before: Sunday.' Feedback is in a polite live region.

readability.evidence: Kid text is four short paragraphs of 4 to 10 word sentences using the target words first, next, last, before, after, morning, afternoon, evening, yesterday, today and tomorrow, passing the family kid FK limit; lab prompts are one line for a parent to read aloud. The adult text quotes the statutory wording and names three mistakes.

no_filler.evidence: Each kid paragraph teaches one group of words (sequence, before/after, parts of the day, the three days). The adult side gives the curriculum link, the key point about spoken order versus real order, the mistakes and what the lab does. The content gate's filler patterns passed and the family tip is a bedtime retell and a dressing game.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots in light and dark (r1403/order-phone-*) show every card's drawn picture and label inside its slot, slot labels above, and the completed row. Cards are at least 70 px wide even with four slots; the young class gives 56 px buttons for every card ('Put Seed in First'), so nothing needs fine dragging. The walk gate passed all 5 tasks on phone and desktop.

accessibility.evidence: axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13. Every drag has a labelled button, the canvas aria-label updates after each placement and on completion lists the whole order ('In order! First: Seed. Next: Shoot. Last: Flower.'), and Challenge answers are real buttons in a labelled group with a polite live region.
